angle: the material the sound acts on, seen close: one water surface that the four waveforms cross as four wave trains
drawing_language: edge-lit silhouette: a 3D heightfield sliced into rows of constant depth and projected through one low camera, each row a black mass with a dark hairline rim, the crest tops that nothing nearer hides lit as short grey lips (brighter the taller and nearer), and the front row's whole edge the one brightest line
subject: A low, close view across a water surface where four wave trains, one per waveform (sine, triangle, square, saw), arrive from four directions and cross, the crests catching a light along their edges.
controls: morph moves the mixing window across the four trains, so the dominant swell changes direction and crest shape as it turns: long smooth head-on rows (sine), peaked diagonal ridges (triangle), flat-topped plateaus (square), long ramps that break off in cliffs (saw).
overlap lets the other trains into the surface, so clean parallel ridges break into a crossing, choppy lattice where crests meet and stack.
spread pulls the trains' wavelengths apart, so the crossing pattern drifts into a moire of tall chop and flat calm patches that beat across the surface.
tone sets how many harmonics each train keeps, so crests go from soft rounded swells at 0 to sharp knife-edged lips at 100, with more and narrower lit edges.
skew moves each shaped train's breakpoint, so sine and triangle crests lean over into ramps and the square's plateaus narrow to thin spikes; the saw train doesn't change.
phase slides each train against the one before, so where they overlap the tall crossing peaks move and fill or hollow out; with one train sounding the surface stays as it is.
reference: opxy/reference/field-and-figure.jpg (one subject filling the body, quiet ground); library/theseus-tower for a modelled 3D form drawn in grey line under the two-page header
risks: Sliced heightfields are close to the familiar 'ridgeline' or terrain-plot look; without the lit lips and the four-direction crossing it could read as a landscape or any synth's waveform plot rather than this machine's four trains.
Which train is which is told only by direction and crest shape; at overlap 100% the four merge and no single waveform is legible, which is honest to the sound but harder to read.

Every control rewrites the whole surface: 12 row masses of up to 62 points plus ~30 lip ribbons are all static artwork in the sketch. On the device this needs either pre-drawn variants or a handful of mutable outlines (max 4 paths x 64 points), so the row count would have to shrink a lot, which is the main fight with the direction.
Phase only shows with overlap open; at the default (one train plus a touch of its neighbours) it moves very little and may fail the perceptibility floor.
The sine train comes head-on and at morph 0 the surface is a calm, almost flat swell with few lit lips: correct, but the quietest frame of the set.
The note response isn't designed yet; the natural one is the surface swelling (row amplitude) and the lips brightening while notes are held.
